paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's promise and our part go together. Paul has a word from God that not a single hair of anybody's head will be lost (Acts 27:34), and he STILL tells the centurion, "Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved" (Acts 27:31). Trusting God doesn't mean sitting on your hands. It means doing the next sensible thing while you hold on to what He said.

Look at what Paul does when everybody is scared. He takes bread, gives thanks to God in front of them all, and eats (Acts 27:35). Then they were all encouraged (Acts 27:36). I think that's a quiet kind of courage, friend. Your faith doesn't have to be loud to be seen, because people notice when you thank God and keep going on a rough day.

And then the ship breaks up, and nobody gets in on style points. Planks, broken pieces, whatever floats, and "everyone was brought safely to land" (Acts 27:44). I think that's good news for the day your plans fall apart. God's rescue doesn't need your plan to survive, and I'd float in on a plank any day to prove it. This voyage isn't over yet, so keep the ovens warm.
